newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Latin American ADRs rebound.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Latin American ADRs rebound.

text.p: Latin American shares moved slightly higher on Tuesday on moderate volume, rebounding from the previous day's sluggish activity, traders said.
"We are really up across the board," a trader of American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) said, adding that Mexican and Brazilian stocks were especially firm.
He said the market welcomed the news that Mexico's president fired the attorney general: "Some people are viewing it as positive and that it means making some headway."

But others said the market in fact dropped on Monday afternoon amid concerns over the move. James Barrineau, a Smith Barney analyst, said in a research summary that the replacement of Attorney General Antonio Lozano Gracia "is almost certainly a market negative."
Still, Mexico's ADRs rose, with Telmex gaining 3/8 to 30-7/8 and Transportacion Maritima Mexicana rising 1/4 to 7-1/4.
Brazil's Telebras gained 1/2 to 77-3/4 and Argentina's Telecom Argentina rose 3/4 to 41.
Overall, European ADRs were mixed in light trading volume, traders said.
Philips Electronics NV gained 3/4 to 40-5/8 in early afternoon activity after news reports of a company plan to invest about $1.5 billion in Asia over the next five years.
